acceptance: A lane whose plan needs a protected path gets no ACS predicate on that path (cycle 1788 replay: 007/008 become console follow-ups)
Triage's premise check names a protected path that only a build-plan step mentions
The TDD persona states the rule, and the check is code, not only prose
fix: Triage's premise check covers every path in Scout's build plan, including 'wire into' steps, not only targetFiles; TDD checks each path an AC needs changed against the protected-surface rule (guards.IsProtectedScope) and records an AC on a protected path as a console follow-up instead of a lane predicate.
summary: Cycle 1788's lane contract was unsatisfiable by construction: predicates 007 and 008 required CLI wiring in go/internal/cli/guardcmd/eval.go, a protected surface (integrity_surface.go:40). The builder wired it, was refused, restored the file, and could never turn those predicates green. Triage's premise check looked only at the target directory, not at Scout's build-plan steps ('wire into pre-flight').
title: TDD and triage keep lane ACS predicates off protected paths; an AC that needs one becomes a console follow-up
